items.title: Settings & audit
items.goal: Any recruiter can adjust stage limits at default, client and job level and maintain the Singapore public-holiday list, and every change is tied to the name they typed. With no sign-in, that typed name and its change log are the whole audit trail, so they must be complete.
prd: Users → Settings (decided): any recruiter can change stages, time limits and retention; each change is logged with the name the recruiter types → decided
Users → the portal asks for a recruiter's name before their first change on a device, and remembers it there → decided
Pipeline tracking → Time limits (decided): job over client over default; limits count Singapore working days → decided
UI design → Settings: stage limits by default, client and job; public holidays; change log → decided
Data model → stage_limits, sg_public_holidays, settings_log → suggested
exit: Limits can be set at all three levels and take effect on candidates already in a stage
Public holidays can be added and removed, and working-day counts follow immediately
Every settings change appears in the change log with the typed name and a Singapore timestamp
No change of any kind can be saved without a typed name
outOfScope: User accounts, roles or permissions — the MVP has no sign-in
Retention settings, which belong to the real-data release
Holidays for any country other than Singapore

items.title: Recruiters adjust stage limits at every level
items.story: As a recruiter, I want to give a slow client a longer limit without changing it for everyone, so that the overdue list stays worth reading.
ac: Given the settings screen, when I change a default, client or job limit, then it is saved and my typed name is recorded.
Given candidates already in a stage, when a limit changes, then their status is recomputed against the new limit rather than a snapshot.
Given a limit that is not a positive whole number of working days, when I try to save it, then the save is refused with a clear message.
prd: Users → Settings (decided): any recruiter can change limits; each change is logged with the typed name → decided
Pipeline tracking → Time limits: a job's limit overrides the client's, which overrides the default → decided
UI design → Settings: stage limits by default, client and job → decided

items.title: Build the settings screen for stage limits with change logging
items.what: Build the limits part of Settings from `design/specs/settings.md`: default limits, per-client limits and per-job limits, each save validated, logged to `settings_log` with the typed name, and visibly showing which level a limit came from.
scope: A route and page with the three levels, showing the effective limit and where it came from
A Server Action with Zod validation writing the limit and a `settings_log` row with the typed name
Failing tests first: a non-positive or fractional limit is refused; a saved limit changes the effective value for candidates already in the stage; every save writes exactly one log row
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover invalid values, effect on in-flight candidates and the single log row
The screen shows the effective limit and which level supplied it
Every save records the typed recruiter name
Playwright passes at desktop and phone width

items.title: Recruiters maintain the Singapore public holidays
items.story: As a recruiter, I want to add next year's public holidays myself, so that the overdue list does not start counting Chinese New Year as working days.
ac: Given the holidays list, when I add a date with a name, then working-day counts skip it from that moment.
Given an existing holiday, when I remove it, then the change is logged with my typed name.
Given a date that is already a holiday, when I add it again, then it is refused rather than duplicated.
prd: Pipeline tracking → Time limits: working days skip Singapore public holidays → decided
UI design → Settings: public holidays → decided

items.title: Build the public-holiday list with add and remove
items.what: Add the holidays section to Settings: list by year, add a date with a name, remove one, and log every change with the typed name — with working-day counts picking the change up immediately.
scope: Holidays listed by year on the settings screen
Add and remove Server Actions with Zod validation, each writing a `settings_log` row
Failing tests first: a duplicate date is refused; adding a holiday changes a working-day count that spans it; removing one changes it back
Playwright coverage of add and remove
exclusions: Importing a holiday calendar from an external source
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover the duplicate refusal and the effect of adding and removing on a working-day count
Every add and remove writes a log row with the typed name
Playwright covers adding and removing a holiday at both widths

items.title: Every change is tied to a typed name
items.story: As the agency director, I want every stage move and settings change to carry a name, so that with no sign-in we can still reconstruct who changed what.
ac: Given my first change on this device, when I act, then the portal asks for my name before the change is saved.
Given I have given my name, when I make further changes on that device, then it is not asked for again but is still recorded.
Given a blank or whitespace-only name, when I try to save it, then it is refused.
Given the change log, when I open it, then every settings change shows its name, what changed and when, in Singapore time.
prd: Users → Audit trail: actions are tied to a typed name, not a verified person → decided
Users → the portal asks for the name before a recruiter's first change on a device and remembers it there → decided
UI design → Settings: change log → decided

items.title: Implement typed-name capture, validation and device persistence
items.what: Make the typed name a single shared mechanism every change path uses: ask once per device, validate it, remember it locally, allow it to be changed, and make it impossible to write an audited change without it. Test-first, because this is the entire audit trail.
scope: A shared hook and server-side validator for the recruiter name

Failing tests first: blank and whitespace-only names are refused; an over-long name is refused; the name persists on the device and is not asked for again; changing the name updates it and later records use the new one; a server action that writes an audited row without a name fails
Used by the stage move, the profile edit, the flag resolve and every settings action
No storage of the name on the server beyond the audit rows themselves
exclusions: Any sign-in or identity verification — the MVP has none
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover blank, whitespace, over-long, persistence, change of name, and the server-side refusal
Every audited write path goes through the one validator, proven by a test that a new path without it fails
The name is remembered on the device and never stored server-side except in audit rows

items.title: Build the change-log view
items.what: Show the settings change log on the Settings screen: what changed, from what to what, who typed their name and when, in Singapore time, newest first and filterable.
scope: A paginated log view reading `settings_log`, newest first
Per entry: the setting, old and new values, the typed name, and the Singapore-time timestamp
Filters by setting type and by name
exclusions: Stage-change history, which lives on the candidate profile
Exporting the log — that is a real-data release concern
Editing or deleting log entries — the log is append-only
done: Every settings change appears with its old and new values, the typed name and a Singapore-time timestamp
The log is append-only: no UI path edits or deletes an entry
Filters by setting type and by name work, covered by an end-to-end test
Playwright passes at desktop and phone width
